candidates.name: Iran-Iraq Gas Pipeline (Basra)
candidates.sponsor: National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC) / Iraq Ministry of Electricity
candidates.from: IGAT-6 at Ahvaz via Shalamcheh (Khorramshahr) border crossing, Iran

evidence.note: NIGC and Iraq's Ministry of Electricity signed a SECOND gas export contract (Nov 2015) specifically for Basra: 7 mcm/d initially, ramping to 20-35 mcm/d (35 mcm/d peak in the five hot months), for power generation — a separate deal from the 2013 Baghdad contract.

Iran exporting 32 mcm/d to Iraq; commitments cover both Baghdad (plus Diyala) AND the southern city of Basra — confirming two distinct delivery obligations/lines; Basra deliveries began after the Baghdad line (EIA and trade press date first Basra flows to mid-2018).

candidates.why_maybe_new: There are physically two Iranian export lines into Iraq: Naft Shahr->Baghdad/Diyala (2013 contract) and Shalamcheh->Basra (2015 contract, flows from ~July 2018). The roster carries only one generic entry, P5855 'Iran-Iraq Gas Pipeline' (cap=35.00), which can only cover one of them. If P5855 is the Baghdad line, the Basra line is missing (and vice versa). Borderline match to P5855 — consolidator should check which border crossing P5855's route uses.

candidates.name: Kurdistan-Turkey Gas Export Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Kurdistan Regional Government (domestic trunkline build-out contracted to KAR Group, 2021)
candidates.from: KRG gas network at Duhok (fed from Khor Mor via Erbil)
candidates.to: Turkish border at Fishkhabour (onward tie-in to Turkey's grid)

evidence.note: KRG Ministry of Natural Resources publication: under the Nov 2013 KRG-Turkey package of agreements, KRG to export >10 bcm/y of gas to Turkey via a dedicated export pipeline, with a new KRG metering station north of the federal Fishkhabour station; first exports were then targeted for 2016 (never realized). Page live and describes the export line as distinct from the domestic Khor Mor-Erbil network.

Analysis (Jul 8, 2025): 2021 KAR Group contract to expand the network from PUK-area fields to Erbil and onward to Dohuk near the Turkish border, with the ultimate goal of connecting to Turkish infrastructure for export; project stalled by KDP-PUK dispute but export ambition still live.

Iraq Oil Report (Feb 3, 2022): the new 52-inch line extending toward the Turkish border is being built 'with extra capacity for more destinations in the future, including potential exports' — i.e., the domestic Erbil-Duhok segment is sized for a future cross-border export leg.

candidates.why_maybe_new: Roster covers the domestic KRG segments only — P4047 Khormor-Erbil (construction, 36in) and P4053 Erbil-Duhok (construction, 52in) — both terminating inside Iraq. The cross-border leg from Duhok to Fishkhabour and into Turkey (the actual export interconnector under the 2013 KRG-Turkey framework) is not in the roster. GEM may track it as a Turkey-side project; consolidator should check the Turkey roster before adding.

candidates.name: Iraq-Jordan Gas Pipeline (Basra-Aqaba gas leg)
candidates.sponsor: Iraq Ministry of Oil / Government of Jordan
candidates.to: Ma'an-Aqaba, Jordan (tie-in to the Arab Gas Pipeline planned)

evidence.note: April 2013 Iraq-Jordan agreement for an $18bn twin pipeline Basra->Aqaba: 1 million bpd crude PLUS a parallel natural gas line to supply Jordan (~258 MMcf/d on the Jordanian stretch).
Pipeline Technology Journal: Jordan approved construction of the new oil AND gas double pipeline from Basra to Aqaba.
Rudaw (Feb 2018): Iraqi cabinet re-approved the Basra-Aqaba project as a twin oil and gas pipeline — brief revival of the gas leg before the project was again downscoped to oil-only.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No Jordan-touching gas line exists in the roster. Distinct from P7573 Basra-Ceyhan (Turkey direction) and from the Basra-Aqaba OIL pipeline (oil tracker, not gas roster). The gas leg was dropped in the 2017 downscoping and the project is now pursued as oil-only, so status is cancelled/shelved — GEM does track cancelled cross-border proposals (cf. P0450, P0481).

candidates.name: Akkas-Syria Gas Pipeline
candidates.sponsor: Iraq Ministry of Oil (Akkas development now with SLB, drilling from Jan 2026)
candidates.from: Akkas gas field, al-Anbar province, Iraq (near Al-Qa'im / Syrian border)
candidates.to: Arab Gas Pipeline in Syria (Homs area), onward toward Turkey/Europe

evidence.note: Syria-in-Figures analysis: the Akkas Gas Pipeline (aka Iraq-Europe Gas Pipeline), planned as early as 2009, would run from Akkas in al-Anbar through Syria to connect to the Arab Gas Pipeline and on to Turkey/Europe; stalled by the Syrian war and ISIS's 2014 seizure of Akkas, but listed among corridors under renewed post-Assad discussion; SLB began drilling at Akkas Jan 2026.

In September 2004 Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Lebanon agreed to connect the Arab Gas Pipeline with Iraq's gas grid to allow Iraqi gas exports toward Europe — the long-standing framework for an Iraq-Syria gas interconnection.

candidates.why_maybe_new: No Iraq-Syria gas line in the roster: P0450 (Iran-Iraq-Syria 'Friendship' line, cancelled) is a different project carrying Iranian gas, and P1841 Baiji-K3-Al Kaem terminates at Al-Qa'im inside Iraq. The Akkas->AGP export link is a separate, never-captured cross-border proposal, newly relevant given Akkas development restarting (2026) and post-Assad AGP revival talk.
